input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together in a playground. Each of you is running, jumping, and doing different things at the same time.

Now, how does the playground "know" where everyone is and what everyone is doing, so that you all see each other moving around correctly?

Well, imagine there is a super-fast helper (called a "server") that lives on the internet. Every time you move or do something in the game, your computer quickly tells the helper, "I jumped!" or "I ran that way!" The helper then tells all your friends’ computers, "He jumped!" so everyone sees you jump at the same time.

This helper is super fast and works all the time, making sure everyone’s game looks the same and nobody is running through walls or missing from the game.

That’s how games like CoD or WoW let lots of people play together and see each other doing things at the same time!
